text:
maria_ops: Heads-up: transit provider in eu-west3 has a maintenance window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. They warned about intermittent BGP flaps. We're planning a staggered maintenance to avoid large capacity spikes. Affects ~120 GPUs (≈6% prod).

maria_ops: Proposal: 4 cohorts, 30m drain + 10m reboot + 20m validation each. Start at 01:45 UTC canaries in small pool, then cohorts every 25m to overlap warmup. Total wall ~3h.

zach_infra: ok. can we reduce blast radius by isolating tenant-affine racks? we should push priority-tenants to other regions for that window.

liam_sre: +1. Also recommend increasing healthcheck retries in routing for 10m after each cohort to avoid premature failovers.

anya_prod: Do we need to proactively message Dedicated customers? any SLA risk?

maria_ops: yes, Dedicated customers with reserved racks in eu-west3: we'll send comms now. No SLA breach expected if we follow cohort plan and fallbacks. ops on call will own comms if any rollback.

kai_eng: For cache/KV concerns: we'll lose prefix cache for drained nodes. Plan to run kv-seed after each reboot:
```
# seed command (run from ops box)
./tools/kv-seed --pool eu-west3-cohort-1 --shards 8 --parallel 4
```
Run at T+5m after node becomes Ready.

zach_infra: Also pre-warm model weights to avoid cold-start token latency. Use smaller quantized variant for canary traffic: model=redwood-quant-small for 10% of canary traffic.

liam_sre: routing change snippet:
```
POST /routing/update
{ "route": "eu-west3", "health_retries": 6, "fallback": "eu-west1,eu-central" }
```
We'll apply with a short TTL.

maria_ops: Capacity plan: we have 2 spare racks in eu-west1 and 1 in eu-central we can burst to. Expected request shift will be ~8% increase in those regions. Ops-runbook updated with backfill steps.

anya_prod: Cost note — bursting to eu-west1 will hit cross-region egress and may increase monthly by ~$3.5k if sustained. Should we cap burst?

maria_ops: We'll cap automated burst to 50 GPUs concurrently and enable a token-rate limit for non-critical routes. That keeps cost ~=1.2k estimate.

kai_eng: Small checklist:
- set canary weight 5% -> 10% if green
- kv-seed at +5m
- prefix-cache warm with sample prompts
- disable large-batch autoscaling for 15m during cohort
- enable extra logging on token-latency metrics

zach_infra: one more: node-drain command we run is:
```
kubectl drain gpu-node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
Make sure jobs flagged as "interruptible=false" are migrated first.

liam_sre: On-call rota: kai_eng covers cohort1, zach_infra cohort2, mariar_ops cohort3, liam_sre cohort4. ops-bot will post reminders.

ops-bot: Scheduled event created: "eu-west3 transit maintenance - staged node drain" 2026-06-12 01:45 UTC -> 04:00 UTC. Reminder 30m prior. :calendar:

anya_prod: I'll draft the customer note (short) and post to #customer-success for review.

maria_ops: Thanks — if no objections by EOD we'll proceed. If anyone sees high-risk tenants we missed ping me directly. :thumbsup:

zach_infra: ack. I'll pre-stage scripts & monitor netctl counters.

liam_sre: ack. I'll bump alert thresholds and add a transient runbook for BGP flap noise.

kai_eng: ack, will add kv-seed job to CI ops-playbooks and test locally now.

maria_ops: final note: during canary window, if tail latency spikes > 2x baseline for 5m we abort and roll back to previous routing.

zach_infra: got it. adding healthcheck monitor rule now.

maria_ops: thanks everyone.
